nodes.description: Biallelic severe NEU1 variants abolish lysosomal neuraminidase-1 (exo-alpha-sialidase) activity. In congenital and severe type II sialidosis, mutant NEU1 proteins are catalytically inactive and either retained in pre-lysosomal compartments with defective lysosomal targeting (Class I) or transported to lysosomes without enzymatic activity (Class II).

nodes.description: Enlargement of the spleen due to reticuloendothelial lysosomal storage and splenic extramedullary hematopoiesis; reported across type II sialidosis (often as combined hepatosplenomegaly at birth in congenital cases, and in 2/7 patients in the cited infantile/juvenile type II cohort, where individual features are documented in patients surviving past the neonatal period).

evidence.snippet: All patients with type II disease have, among other symptoms, coarse face, enlargement of spleen and liver, dysostosis multiplex, vertebral deformities, and severe mental retardation.

evidence.reference_title: Sialidosis type II: Expansion of phenotypic spectrum and identification of a common mutation in seven patients.
evidence.snippet: The accumulation of sialated glycopeptides and oligosaccharides in the liver and the spleen leads to their enlargement.

nodes.description: Intrauterine fetal demise or perinatal death shortly after delivery resulting from fulminant systemic hydrops fetalis.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenesis, Emerging therapeutic targets and Treatment in Sialidosis.
evidence.snippet: Type II patients with the most acute, congenital form of the disease develop hydrops fetalis, neonatal ascites, or both; they are stillborn or die shortly after birth with a systemic and fulminant condition.

nodes.description: Progressive intralysosomal accumulation of sialylated glycopeptides and oligosaccharides in hepatocytes, Kupffer cells, and splenic macrophages produces visceral organ enlargement including congenital hepatosplenomegaly, hepatomegaly, and splenomegaly.
